figure_description:
Two population pyramid graphs side by side under the heading "Comparison of Age Structure Between Country X and Country Y". Both graphs have a vertical axis on the left labeled "Ages" with tick marks from 0 to 89 in increments of 5 (0, 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, 39, 44, 49, 54, 59, 64, 69, 74, 79, 84, 89). A central vertical line divides "Males" on the left from "Females" on the right. The horizontal axis at the bottom is labeled "Percent of Population" with tick marks numbered 8 down to 0 on the left side and 0 up to 8 on the right side.

The left graph is subtitled "Country X Age Distribution / Rapid Growth". It forms a wide-based pyramid. The base (age 0) extends to approximately 7% on both the male and female sides. At age 19, it is about 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 1.5% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

The right graph is subtitled "Country Y Age Distribution / Slow Growth". It has a much narrower base and more vertical sides. At age 0, it extends to about 3% for males and 3% for females. At age 19, it is slightly below 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 2% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

Below the graphs is a key with three boxes:
- A solid dark gray box labeled "Ages 0–19 Going to have children", corresponding to the shaded bottom section (ages 0 to 19) in both graphs.
- An unshaded white box labeled "Ages 20–44 Having children", corresponding to the unshaded middle section (ages 20 to 44) in both graphs.
- A diagonally hatched box labeled "Ages 45–89 Finished having children", corresponding to the hatched top section (ages 45 to 89) in both graphs.
accessibility_text:
Two graphs for the comparison of age structure between country x and country y. The x axis of both graphs shows percent of population, 0 to 8 percent, and the y-axis of both graphs is age, from 0 to 89. Each graph shows males and females separately, though the age structure is the same. Each graph indicates the proportion that are age 0 to 19, who are going to have children, those who are age 20 to 44, who are having children, and those age 45 to 89, who have finished having children. Country x age distribution shows rapid growth, where the younger ages are a greater percentage of the population than those who are older. Country y shows slow growth, where the older ages are an equal or greater percentage of the population than those who are younger. Country X has a larger percentage of people in the “having children” or “going to have children” categories than does country Y.
The graphs for Country X and Country Y show the age structure of each country’s population. The population is divided into three age groups from youngest to oldest. The graphs enable predictions about population growth.
